title: Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage — Reconciling Estimated Months After Approval
content:
Once eligibility is approved, every month billed as an estimate is reconciled to the actual patient pay of the month. This is a rule of Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage for cases whose application was pending and has now been approved.

## Governing clauses

- Where the actual patient pay of the month is lower than the estimates billed for it, the estimate is reduced by the difference with reason `trueup_decrease`, the actual patient pay of a reconciled estimate month being the lesser of the patient pay the notice sets for that month and the month's cost of care; this holds for the latest month billed as an estimate, by service month, on a case whose eligibility has been approved (a case in status eligible; on a case in any other status this reconciliation reduces nothing), and only for such a month; every other reconciliation remains under the base rule: within the trueup days after the approval notice, where the actual patient pay exceeds the estimates billed for the month the difference is billed with charge basis "true-up increase", and where it is lower the estimate is reduced by the difference with reason `trueup_decrease`.
- For an actual-billed month that the actual-month review prices, a reconciled estimate month that the estimate reconciliation prices and a pending estimate month that the pending-month review prices, the month's cost of care is the cost of care that review's own pricing gives, and only for such a month; every other month remains under the base rule, where the month's cost of care is the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate.
- For a reconciled estimate month that the estimate reconciliation prices and a pending estimate month that the pending-month review prices, a month of admission, discharge or death takes the cost of care that review's own pricing gives in place of the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate, and only for such a month; every other month of admission, discharge or death remains under the base rule: in a month of admission, discharge or death, patient pay is the lesser of the monthly patient pay and the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate, with charge basis "partial month", and any amount already billed above that is reduced with reason `cost_of_care_cap`.
- A charge is reduced once per adjustment reason.

## The posting tool

**What it does.** `post_trueup_decrease_6ec57e06` posts a reduction against one estimated patient pay charge of an approved case on a Medical Assistance case: it lowers what the named charge asks of the resident by the amount given and records the reduction, with the reason given, on the case's billing record for the same service month as the charge. The case's patient pay balance falls by the same amount, so a charge that was already paid leaves a credit the resident or representative can see on the case.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: unlock `post_trueup_decrease_6ec57e06` with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`, then call it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

- `medicaid_case_id` — the reference number of the resident's Medical Assistance case whose charge is reduced, as returned by the case lookup (identifier).
- `charge_entry_id` — the reference number of the estimated patient pay charge being reduced, as returned by the case billing-record lookup for that case (identifier).
- `adjustment_reason` — the controlled reason recorded on the reduction, one of: `trueup_decrease` (an estimate billed during the pending period is lowered to the month's reconciled actual patient pay), `patient_pay_redetermined` (a charge is lowered because a County Assistance Office redetermination set a lower patient pay for that month), `not_eligible_month` (an estimate for a month outside the eligibility period is taken off), `cost_of_care_cap` (a month's patient pay is lowered to the month's cost of care), `billing_error` (a charge billed in a wrong amount is corrected).
- `amount` — the reduction in US dollars: a positive number with 2 decimal places (cents), rounded half up to the cent, with no currency symbol and no thousands separator.

**Return.** A receipt with status posted completes the call. It lists `entry_id` (the new reduction entry), `medicaid_case_id`, `charge_entry_id`, `service_month` (YYYY-MM), `adjustment_reason`, `amount` (two decimals), `entry_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `patient_pay_balance` (two decimals with the reduction posted; a leading minus sign means a credit) and status. An amount that is not a positive figure is refused with an error and nothing is recorded.
